pull_request_lookup_failed.now: could not read merged pull requests (gh: simulated failure); using ancestry alone
pull_request_lookup_failed.why: The port names why the lookup failed, which the shell version never did. Carried over from tests/gh/test_output_parity.py's DIVERGENCES table unchanged: the reason now reaches the line from GhError rather than from the Python's gh_json, and reads the same.

operation_in_progress_in_a_linked_worktr.why: #218 finding 6: the linked-worktree in-progress check moved from readWorktrees into preflight, before the fetch and the advance. The shell version, and the port until now, ran the check too late, so a repository otherwise ready to advance reported it as up to date before it skipped. The check now fires on sight, the same as the check for this checkout's own in-progress marker, and the advance line never prints.

lock_file_changed.why: pnpm only (ruling, 2026-09-20). The scenario's subject is a lock file the pull touched; the port watches one lock file, so the scenario builds that one. The reported line is unchanged, which is why the golden still applies.

lock_file_untouched.why: Same substitution. The state being asserted is a pull that did NOT touch the watched lock file, which needs the watched lock file to exist to mean anything.

notInTheTable.cannot list worktrees: tests/gh/test_output_parity.py records it: `git worktree list` failing left the shell version with an empty branch-to-worktree map, so it never printed a skip. The Python raises the skip the shell version meant to and the port keeps the Python's behaviour. There is no scenario for it in bash-output.json at all.

ghVocabulary.why: gh-sync-repo.py:263 to 290 spells six reasons a gh call could not be read. The port keeps three of them in the Python's words, 'gh is not on PATH' (off status 127), 'gh exited <n>' and 'gh returned rows that are not pull requests' (its own check on the rows), and reads the rest off GhError.detail, which is gh's own account without the 'gh <argv> failed: ' prefix the message carries, because lib/gh.ts owns that vocabulary now. Each line below is what the report says instead of what the Python said for the SAME state. They are recorded here rather than only in a test so that a change to the vocabulary has to be recorded to stay green; sync-repo.merge-proof.test.ts drives its example from this list, taking 'message' as the error the real client throws and 'account' as the part of it the report quotes. A gh that a SIGNAL ended is listed too: subprocess reports that as a negative returncode, so the Python prints 'gh exited -15' where lib/gh.ts names the signal, which is the same complaint gh-sync.py:147 to 158 makes about negative statuses in its own report. accountOf's remaining arm, a pipe that failed ("gh's output could not be read: ..."), is deliberately NOT listed: subprocess.run surfaces no pipe error, so the Python cannot reach that state at all, and a table of what the report says INSTEAD of what the Python said for the SAME state has no row for a state the Python has not got.

inProcessFanOut.why:
The fan-out is in-process (the design ruling in the approved plan), so a job has no exit status of its own, cannot be killed by a signal and cannot fail to start. It can still throw. gh-sync.py:123 to 135 folds a child that raised into THAT repository's section so the other sections survive; the port does the same with the line below, which replaces the three the child process took with it. The Python's first line carries the repository's basename (gh-sync.py:135 builds 'basename
  ✗ could not start the sync script: ...' as one string) because a child that never ran wrote no heading of its own; the port writes that same heading ahead of the line below whenever the job threw before its first line, so a section is never left sitting under the previous repository's name.
was: ✗ could not start the sync script: <error>

exitStatus.why: gh-sync.sh dropped the single-repository path's child status at its lines 72 to 73, so that path always exited 0, whatever a job answered or threw. #81 (round 7) made a throw exit 1 there instead, once every report line had been written; #218 finding 8 later removed the RepoJob arm that answered a non-zero status without throwing, because syncRepo never produced one. Only the throw half of this divergence still holds.
exitStatus.was: always exits 0, whatever a job answered or threw
exitStatus.now: exits 1 when a job threw; a skipped repository still answers 0

failureSummary.why: The stderr line `failed(...)` carries once every report line is on stdout: how many repositories failed, of how many were tried. New with #81; there is no shell or Python line it replaces, so this is a statement of the new contract rather than a table of substitutions.
